title: Your fairness may vary: Pretrained language model fairness in toxic text classification
findings: The study found that fairness concerning the 'religion' group in toxic text classification varies significantly more than accuracy, depending on the language model, training data size, and random initialization seed. There was no clear correlation between model size and fairness. For example, on the Jigsaw dataset with the BERT model, the baseline equalized odds violation was high for the general religion group (0.18) and even higher for the Muslim subgroup (0.20). The paper demonstrated that post-processing bias mitigation methods like Fair Score Transformer (FST) can successfully reduce this fairness violation for the religion group and its subgroups with a minimal decrease in model accuracy.

measurement_description: The benchmark measured bias in toxic text classification based on the presence of religious identity terms. It used the 'equalized odds' fairness metric, which quantifies the disparity in true positive and false positive rates for toxicity prediction between texts that mention a religion and texts that do not.
